criteria.justification: The response directly treats the earlier paused launch as evidence that “good mapping accuracy is insufficient” and distinguishes component-level mapping performance from whether the product delivers customer value.

It explicitly says the team’s year of investment “should influence how we transition, not determine what success means,” while preserving the existing infrastructure as a diagnostic and regression tool.

The response acknowledges, “I would not claim we can evaluate that new criterion yet,” then proposes sourcing representative ground truth, testing label feasibility, building a held-out set, and limiting release to a controlled pilot or delaying it meanwhile.

It notes that another year optimizing mapping accuracy would not close the customer-value gap and proposes learning which mapping errors materially affect outcomes so engineering effort is directed toward consequential errors rather than all categorization errors equally.

It clearly makes customer-outcome accuracy primary, retains mapping accuracy as a diagnostic and regression guardrail, and provides a concrete staged transition involving metric definition, ground-truth collection, dual measurement, and evidence-gated release scope.
